issues.failure_explanation: The displayed Gårding inequality is not coercivity or positivity of the form on the whole Hilbert space, and (A3) does not require f' to be nonnegative. The preceding estimate is only an upper bound on the f' term, whereas a lower bound requires controlling its absolute value. Thus convexity and weak lower semicontinuity do not follow from the argument given, so attainment of the Rayleigh infimum and the subsequent strict spectral gap are unproved.

issues.failure_explanation: The Morse–Bott assumption controls the Lagrangian Hessian only on the tangent space. It gives no positivity in the radial direction or on the full H_0^1 space required for P_φ to define a Riemannian metric. Since (A3) permits f' to be negative, E''(φ_g)−λ_g I may have a negative full-space direction, and adding a sufficiently small σ_0 I need not make it coercive. Thus the inverse, metric, and P-RG used by the theorem may be undefined.
